failure_handler_analysis.is_it_wrapped: No -- _map_exception_to_error(payload, exc) reads exc's type/message to choose an error_code, but does not wrap or re-raise a new exception; the original exc object itself is discarded after this function returns (never stored, never re-raised).
failure_handler_analysis.is_valueerror_generated_locally_by_this_: No -- exc is whatever propagated up from run_streaming_tradingagents_research (or run_original_tradingagents_research, not used in these attempts). The handler only inspects its type and str(exc).
failure_handler_analysis.does_cause_context_survive: Not applicable at this boundary -- exc itself (with its own __cause__/__context__, if any) is available in the except block, but the code never accesses or logs __cause__/__context__ here, and exc is discarded once the function returns.
failure_handler_analysis.do_logs_discard_traceback: Yes, deliberately -- routes_research.py:3006's logger.error(...) call has never passed exc_info, and a pre-existing test (tests/test_research_input_validation.py::test_unexpected_internal_failure_is_logged_safely_at_error_level) explicitly pins `records[0].exc_info is None` as intentional behavior for this exact log line. This appears to be a deliberate policy (this boundary log line never carries a traceback, likely to avoid exposing internal call-stack detail in a log that could be shipped to less-trusted aggregators) -- not an oversight to be casually reversed.
failure_handler_analysis.does_job_state_store_only_exc_type_messa: Yes -- the persisted run/job state (surfaced via GET .../status) carries only error_code='INTERNAL_ERROR' and a generic safe message; the run/job record itself never carried the original exception's message or type. The ONLY place `exc_type=ValueError` was ever visible was this one ERROR-level log line's %s-formatted type name -- not the message, not a traceback, not stored in the database.
failure_handler_analysis.confirmed_via_this_tasks_own_attempt_to_: This task initially added exc_info=True to this exact log line, which broke the pre-existing safety test above (a real, caught regression) -- reverted. The correct fix (implemented instead) is to capture the traceback CLOSER TO THE SOURCE, inside run_streaming_tradingagents_research's own new logger, which has no such 'no-traceback' policy attached to it.

recommended_minimal_fix.failure_mechanism: An external network call with no application-level timeout can block the calling thread indefinitely (or for however long the underlying library/OS eventually takes to give up), stalling the entire pre-semantic pipeline before any analyst work or semantic processing begins.
recommended_minimal_fix.why_approximately_903_seconds: Not controlled by this codebase -- an artifact of whatever default the underlying HTTP client/OS eventually imposes on a stalled connection to this specific Yahoo endpoint.
recommended_minimal_fix.external_or_local: The ROOT cause (Yahoo's backend behavior) is external and outside this codebase's control; the FIX (bounding the wait) is entirely local and within this codebase's control.
recommended_minimal_fix.recommended_fix: Wrap this specific call with an explicit, bounded timeout using the same pattern already proven and tested elsewhere in this codebase (comqutor_alpha/structure_engine/week2_llm.py:493's `future.result(timeout=...)` via a ThreadPoolExecutor) -- run `yf.Ticker(...).info` in a bounded worker with a short timeout (e.g. 10-15s, matching this call's own 'best-effort, fail-open' design intent), and on timeout, fall through to the SAME `{}` fallback the function already returns on any other exception -- zero change to the function's documented contract ('best-effort by design... returns {} and the caller falls back to ticker-only context'), only a bound on how long it is allowed to try.
recommended_minimal_fix.semantic_risk: None -- resolve_instrument_identity's own docstring already commits to a fail-open, best-effort contract; timing it out and falling back to {} is not a new behavior, only a bound on an existing one.
recommended_minimal_fix.implementation_risk: Low -- an isolated, single-function change, reusing an existing, already-tested concurrency pattern from this same codebase; does not touch Slice 1/2A/2B, Gold, taxonomy, activation, or conflict logic.
recommended_minimal_fix.why: The fix's correctness (does the timeout actually bound the real stall, and does the pipeline then proceed normally) can only be confirmed by observing a live run complete past this step -- this task explicitly does not implement or validate the fix.
recommended_minimal_fix.timeout_policy_compliance: This is NOT a request to simply increase the existing ~900s boundary -- there is no existing configured boundary to increase. The recommended fix ADDS a new, much SHORTER bound (10-15s) to a call that currently has none, directly addressing the 'unbounded external request' failure mode this task's own policy section calls out.
